title: Grand Jury Rejects DOJ Effort to Indict Key Jan. 6 Witness Cassidy Hutchinson
snippet: Federal prosecutors failed to secure an indictment against former White House aide Cassidy Hutchinson over her high-profile congressional testimony regarding the Jan. 6 Capitol attack.
content:
In a major setback for prosecutors, a federal grand jury has refused to indict Cassidy Hutchinson, a former top aide to Trump White House Chief of Staff Mark Meadows, over her testimony related to the Jan. 6, 2021, Capitol attack.

The decision came after federal litigators presented a proposed indictment to the grand jury, which ultimately declined to concur. The grand jury's refusal to return an indictment marks a rare publicly known defeat for federal prosecutors pursuing high-profile criminal charges tied to the events surrounding the 2020 election fallout.

Explosive Testimony and Political Backlash

Hutchinson became a central and polarizing figure during the 2022 House select committee hearings investigating the Capitol riot. Her televised testimony delivered several shocking revelations about the inner workings of the Trump White House on Jan. 6.

Among her most dramatic claims, Hutchinson testified that President Donald Trump and Meadows were warned that rally attendees were carrying weapons before heading to the Capitol. She also recounted a story allegedly relayed to her by former White House deputy chief of staff Tony Ornato, claiming an enraged Trump tried to grab the steering wheel of the presidential vehicle when told he could not join his supporters at the Capitol. That specific account was later disputed by Trump's driver in separate sworn testimony.

GOP Referral Falls Short

The criminal inquiry into Hutchinson reportedly stemmed from a referral made by House Republican allies of former President Trump, who pushed the Justice Department to scrutinize her statements under oath. The investigation was handled by the Justice Department's Civil Rights Division.

During a court hearing on Tuesday, prosecutor Neville Hedley informed U.S. Magistrate Judge Zia Faruqui that the grand jury had not concurred on a proposed indictment. While Hedley did not name Hutchinson directly in court, multiple sources confirmed she was the target of the grand jury proceedings. The Department of Justice has declined to publicly comment on the outcome.
